author: ojiudezue
title: Only proven code supersedes correct code: layer leak cleanup cut from 4 builds to 1
summary: Operator picked the smaller cleanup cut and added a rule: don't rebuild hardened Tier-3 code that works, be skeptical of other rewrites with clear pro/con, only proven code supersedes correct code. Re-measured every remaining leak; all but one were correct code with no measured defect, so they park with revival triggers. One ~1-day Tier-2 build remains (five identity vetoes that fail open on a second install).
why: The sizing plan priced rewrites by structural cleanliness (guard allowlist rows). Measured: the 'HIGH' security leak fired 6 times in 7 days, all from an iPad tracker since removed, never while armed; no boot AWAY came from the display-entity seed in 27 restarts; phone-left-behind was on 10 min in a week. Rewriting correct access/house-state code to shrink a test allowlist buys no behaviour and adds Tier-3 risk.
alternatives_considered: Option A as first written: 4 builds, ~10 builder-days, guard 256->158
implications: The guard allowlist stays ~257 rows and that is accepted; new consumers must still build on the layer (the guard blocks new leaks). Cleanup items revive only on their measured triggers. The rule applies arc-wide: any plan that replaces working code must show a measured defect and a proven replacement.
revisit_trigger: Security armed with a source_stale arrival row; phone-left-behind on > 2 h/week; a second install; any refactor of the presence privates
